instruction: Rank the four statements from 1 to 4: 1 for the one most like you, 4 for the one least like you. Every number is used once. Think of what you usually do, not what a good trainer should do. There are no better or worse answers.

active.name: Active
active.where: at the top of the circle
active.description: Learns by being inside the experience: taking part, noticing what it is like, and paying attention to the people and the moment. Can move on before making sense of what happened.

reflective.name: Reflective
reflective.where: on the right of the circle
reflective.description: Learns by watching, listening and going back over what happened from more than one point of view. Can hold back a conclusion or a decision for longer than the group needs.

theorist.name: Theorist
theorist.where: at the bottom of the circle
theorist.description: Learns by building an explanation: principles, models and how things connect. Can lose sight of the person or the moment that does not fit the model.

pragmatist.name: Pragmatist
pragmatist.where: on the left of the circle
pragmatist.description: Learns by putting ideas into practice and planning what to do differently. Can adopt what works quickly without asking whether it is the right thing to do.

sets.prompt: A workshop begins with an activity I have never done before.

statements.active: I take part straight away and notice what the experience is like.
statements.reflective: I watch how the first people do it before I join.
statements.theorist: I want to understand the idea behind the activity first.
statements.pragmatist: I want to know how I could use this activity with my own groups.

sets.prompt: I have to prepare a session on a topic that is new to me.

statements.active: I start from a personal experience of the topic, or find a way to have one.
statements.reflective: I start by listening to people who see the topic in different ways.
statements.theorist: I start from the key concepts and how they connect to each other.
statements.pragmatist: I start from activities on this topic that have worked with other groups.

sets.prompt: During a training, my small group starts discussing a sensitive topic.

statements.active: I say what I feel and respond directly to what others share.
statements.reflective: I listen to everyone first and speak after I have heard the different views.
statements.theorist: I try to identify the general principle behind what people are saying.
statements.pragmatist: I suggest that the group focuses on what we could do about it.

sets.prompt: During a session I am running, the group reacts in a way I did not expect.

statements.active: I stop following the plan and respond to how people are feeling right now.
statements.reflective: I pause for a moment and observe what is happening before I act.
statements.theorist: I try to understand what explains the reaction before I change anything.
statements.pragmatist: I switch to a different activity and check whether it works better.

sets.prompt: A training event is ending, and I think about what mattered most to me.

statements.active: What mattered most were the moments I experienced together with other people.
statements.reflective: What mattered most was what I noticed by watching and listening to others.
statements.theorist: What mattered most was understanding why some approaches to learning work.
statements.pragmatist: What mattered most were the tools and plans for my next session.

sets.prompt: A session I ran has just ended.

statements.active: I think most about how the session felt, for me and for the group.
statements.reflective: I go through the session step by step to see what happened.
statements.theorist: I look for ideas about learning that explain why it went that way.
statements.pragmatist: I decide on one concrete change for the next time I run it.

sets.prompt: Someone presents a new idea about how people learn.

statements.active: I want to experience the idea in an activity, not only hear it described.
statements.reflective: I want some time to consider it before I form an opinion.
statements.theorist: I check whether the idea is consistent and well argued.
statements.pragmatist: I think about whether it would change anything in my next training.

sets.prompt: My co-trainer and I disagree about how to run an activity.

statements.active: I say how I feel about each option and ask how my co-trainer feels.
statements.reflective: I ask my co-trainer to explain their view fully and listen before I answer.
statements.theorist: I compare both options with what we know about how people learn.
statements.pragmatist: I propose that we try each version once and compare the results.

sets.prompt: A training includes a role-play, and I am one of the players.

statements.active: I let myself get absorbed in my role and in the situation.
statements.reflective: I keep part of my attention on observing how the group behaves.
statements.theorist: I try to identify the general principles the role-play is based on.
statements.pragmatist: I think about how I would adapt this role-play for my own groups.

sets.prompt: I realise that I have made a mistake while facilitating.

statements.active: I pay attention to how the mistake affected the people in the room.
statements.reflective: Afterwards, I review that moment in my mind before I draw any conclusion.
statements.theorist: I try to understand the general cause behind the mistake.
statements.pragmatist: I plan exactly what I will do if the same situation happens again.

sets.prompt: Someone close to me asks what I learned at a training weekend.

statements.active: I tell them about the moments I experienced and what they were like.
statements.reflective: I describe what I noticed about the group and about myself.
statements.theorist: I explain the main ideas and how they connect.
statements.pragmatist: I show them something I am going to do differently from now on.

sets.prompt: I receive written feedback from participants about a session I ran.

statements.active: I pay most attention to the comments about how people felt.
statements.reflective: I read all the comments and compare the different points of view in them.
statements.theorist: I look for a pattern that explains the comments as a whole.
statements.pragmatist: I select the comments that point to changes I can make.
